recipes.name: Baked Stuffed Pasta Shells with Spinach & Tofu "Ricotta"
instructions: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Add the pasta shells and cook for 2 minutes less than the package instructions for al dente. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, warm the oil over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and chili flakes and cook, stirring, for 1 minute, until lightly golden.
Add the passata, basil, and fine sea salt. Reduce the heat to low and cook, uncovered, for about 7 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.
Transfer the sauce to a 9 × 13-inch / 23 × 33cm baking dish.
Position a rack in the upper third of the oven and preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C*.
Transfer the thawed spinach to a sieve set over a bowl and squeeze out any excess water. Reserve 3 tablespoons of the spinach water and set aside**.
In a food processor, blitz the tofu, cashews, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, pepper, nutmeg, fine sea salt, and the 3 tablespoons of reserved spinach water until smooth.
Remove the blades, then mix in the squeezed spinach.
Fill the pasta shells with the tofu mixture, then arrange them over the sauce in the baking dish.
Bake for about 15 minutes, until lightly golden. Serve warm. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † Passata is a smooth, thick tomato sauce made from strained tomatoes without added seasonings, herbs, or spices. * We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection). ** Save the remaining spinach water for soups or smoothies, if desired.
Storage Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. You can freeze the tray before baking, then pop it in the oven for an hour. Broil for 10 extra minutes, and enjoy!
